content.thinking:
I'm planning the monster truck's proportions based on real-world scale—tall tires around 1.67m diameter, overall height near 3.6m, width 3.6m—then setting up the builder with wheels aligned along the X-axis, facing +Z.

For the tires, I'm working out how to orient cylinder geometry along the x-axis with rotation, using low segment counts for a pixel-art feel, and figuring out tread detailing by mapping lug positions around the tire's angular position for alternating dark and light coloring.

Adding tread color variation with dirt speckling, then building out the bulkier tyre geometry: shoulder cylinder, silver hub rim with bead-lock bolts, and a center hub cone...

Now I'm laying out the chassis: ladder frame rails, front/rear axle positions giving a 3.5m wheelbase, wheel track width, axle rod with differential housing, four-link suspension bars, and yellow coilover shocks connecting axles to frame.

I'm making the coil springs out of stacked thin cylindrical rings rather than a true helix, then planning the pickup-style body dimensions — width spanning between the tires, cab/hood/bed sections, and bottom height sitting just above the axles so wheels show beside the body without needing wheel wells.

For body color, I'm designing a procedural paint pattern with a red/orange ramp and flame tongues licking up from the lower front, using a zigzag wave function to define the jagged flame boundary with yellow tips fading to orange.

Still writing flame paint logic...

Now I'm laying out the car body parts as boxes—lower body slab, hood—sizing and positioning each with specific dimensions and heights.

Still blocking out the cab geometry...

Adding silver roll cage sweeps, a glowing light bar on the cab roof, and the front bumper details—black bumper box, pixel-art grille texture, and glowing headlight boxes positioned on either side of center.

Now I'm working out the door decal: drawing a "7" number plate via pixel art with white fill and black outline, placed on both door surfaces. I need to get the plane orientation right so the texture reads correctly from each side when viewed from outside the vehicle.

Skipping fender flares and mud flaps for simplicity. Now I'm working out the frame structure: two box rails running the length of the chassis, positioned between the axles and body mounts, with cross members tying them together, plus suspension links connecting the front axle to the frame rails in a 4-link setup.

Still placing suspension links and drivetrain components...

I'm checking for collisions between the tires and the shock/spring assemblies, adjusting the track width outward to ±1.7 so the shocks at x=±1.08 clear the tire's inner face and the springs don't overlap the body edge.

Checking shock placement more precisely: spring runs from y 0.9 to 1.95 with 9 coil rings, rod visible above. I'm reconsidering overall width scaling—shrinking the track and tyre width so the shock spring doesn't overlap the tyre inner face, adjusting x-offsets to around ±1.6 for track and ±1.08 for the shock itself.

Now I'm working out tyre geometry: using a 24-sided cylinder of radius 0.85 as the tyre, rotating the segments so a flat face contacts the ground instead of a vertex, which affects where the bottom actually touches y=0.

Checking proportions against wheelbase, I notice the front and rear tyres (centered at z ±1.75) stick out past the body's bumper at z=2.3, which looks wrong for a realistic truck silhouette. I'll pull the body ends out to roughly ±2.35 and bring the wheel positions in to about ±1.55 so the tyres tuck under the body properly.

Planning the chrome exhaust pipes rising behind the cab with angled tips, then sketching rear details: roll cage, light bar, antenna flag, tow hooks, mud flaps, mirrors, door handles, taillights, and a chrome blower with belts. I'll keep the glass simple and opaque, skipping interior detail to avoid overcomplicating it.

Now I'm figuring out the sloped windshield by extruding a side-profile polygon along the cab's thickness, defining the (z,y) outline points for the cab body and windshield angle before extending to the rear window shape.

I'm now working out how to paint the glass versus body panels based on surface normal direction and position, using normal tilt thresholds to detect the sloped windshield face and y/x ranges to mark window regions versus pillars.

Still working out the cab profile...

I'm defining a bodyColor function so cab paint reuses the same body coloring logic. Then I'm sizing the paint texture resolution, estimating painted surface area across tyres and body panels to figure out a reasonable texel density, landing on roughly 1cm cells and weighing 2048 vs 4096 atlas sizes.

Settling on default 1024 texture but using finer 0.04 cells for tyres and 0.05 for the body. I'm also reasoning through how tyre cylinder geometry's smooth radial normals get snapped to axis directions for the pixel-paint grid, working out how cells map onto the tread surface along the cylinder's length and circumference.

Working out the paint logic per tyre face by finding the local offset from center, classifying points as sidewall caps versus tread based on normal direction, then building radial rings for the sidewall black ramp and shoulder lugs, with angular blocks creating a chevron tread pattern using modulo arithmetic on the angle.

Simplifying: I'll reuse the same paint function for both tyre and rim, with concentric zones for dark hub cap, gold accent, silver dithered shading, and a beadlock band near the edge, plus a slightly raised beadlock ring geometry and bolts on top.

Now I'm adding dark wedge slots in the rim's spoke region using an angular modulo check, giving it a five-spoke cutout look. For the tread, I'm mixing in random mud-brown speckles on the lower portion of the tire and body to simulate dirt splatter, using a color ramp with threshold-based snapping for crisp pixel color bands.

I'm keeping the flat color palette tight, defining a small set of named hex constants like chrome, steel, black, yellow, and red, staying under a reasonable color budget. Now I'm setting up the builder with the truck's name and paint size, then starting the import statements for the geometry construction script.

Writing builder imports...

Defining color ramps...

Still shaping the flame tongues...

I'm defining a depth value measuring how far inside the flame a point sits, then mapping that depth to color bands: yellow deep inside, orange in the middle, red near the edges, adjusting for realistic-looking flame coloring with hotter tones toward the base.

Now I'm restricting where flames appear on the body — only the lower side panels using a y-cutoff so they don't awkwardly reach the hood — and adding a dark trim strip along the rocker panels and underside for contrast before moving on to the main body colors.

Setting mud probability to darken based on depth, then moving to the cab: defining glass color ramps with diagonal stripe patterns, and figuring out which face normals correspond to cab sides versus windshield for correct coloring.

Now I'm defining window conditions for front, rear, and roof panels based on position and surface normal, plus adding a central racing stripe with a black border across the hood and roof.

For details, I'm planning tires with tread and rims, lug nuts, and beadlock bolts per wheel — though doing 16 bolts per face across 4 wheels adds up fast, so I need to watch the part budget.

I'll merge the bolt geometries per wheel face into single parts using BufferGeometryUtils to keep things efficient, writing a helper function that positions small box "bolts" around a circle at a given radius and offset.

Then I'm planning the rest of the build: hub center caps as gold octagonal cylinders, followed by axles, diffs, links, shocks, driveshaft, steering link, and skid plate, then frame rails and crossmembers, body panels, and finally all the detail pieces -- grille, headlights, bumpers, hood scoop with blower and stacks, light bar, roll bar, mirrors, door handles, skull decals, antenna with flag, exhaust stacks, taillights, license plate, and tow hooks.

I'm adding step bars with diamond-plate texture, a fuel cap, hood hinge lines and hood pins, and a bed area with a textured liner floor, side walls, tailgate, roll bar hoop, spare strap, and a chrome nitrous bottle with a label lying in the bed. I'm planning tailgate decals using a checker or stripe pattern instead of risky pixel text, then setting up a reusable box-geometry helper function to place parts by dimensions, color, and position.

Now I'm working out rotation conventions for cylinder parts and designing pixel textures for the grille — chrome trim rows with alternating dark slats and chrome highlights — sized to fit the hood plane dimensions cleanly.

Placing the grille and headlights on the lower slab's front face: grille centered around y~1.86, z~2.305, flanked by headlight planes at x±0.82 with smaller width and height, keeping proportions consistent with the slab's overall width.

Sketching a rounded 6x6 pixel-art headlight using a yellow border and cream fill, plus a glow effect. Then I'm defining the bumper as a separate box below the grille — repositioning it so it doesn't overlap, with the grille moved up to y~1.93 (height 0.34) and the bumper placed at y~1.67 (height 0.22), extending forward in z, colored black with a diamond-plate texture.

Generating diamond tile pattern...

Mirroring the bumper at the rear, then starting the hood as a flattened box sized roughly 1.9 wide, 0.3 tall, 1.5 deep, positioned toward the front of the body.

Now I'm adding the supercharger assembly on top of the hood: a chrome cylindrical blower case through the surface, a flat black intake scoop with a mesh-textured top plate, a handful of chrome injector stub cones, and a front pulley cylinder for the drive belt.

Then I'm moving on to the hood scoop detail with a dark grille texture on its front face, and designing the light bar on top of the cab as a black box housing six glowing yellow lamp planes.

Now I'm positioning a sun visor above the windshield, working out the tilt rotation so its front edge angles downward correctly.

With that settled, I'm adding mirror arms extending from the cab sides with small chrome mirror boxes at their ends, then placing chrome door handles and sketching in door seam lines within the cab paint.

I'm also planning skull decals for the lower cab doors around y≈2.33, keeping them below the flame zone so they don't overlap, and considering adding larger versions on the bed's side walls too.

Sketching a symmetric pixel-art skull pattern...

That pattern checks out symmetrically, so I'll finalize the skull pixel grid with white and dark navy tones for contrast against blue. Now I'm working out the bed floor geometry with tile dimensions and positioning, plus considering adding a chrome roll bar hoop behind the cab for detail.

Writing roll bar sweep...

Adding exhaust stacks instead, placing chrome swept pipes beside the cab with slight outward bends and flat caps, rather than the bed-mounted bottle idea.

Now I'm adding heat-shield rings around the stacks, then moving on to frame details, a rear tow hook, and a simple striped license plate. I'll place glowing red taillight boxes and a tailgate slab to finish the bed rear.

Next I'm adding a thin chrome flag antenna mounted inside the bed wall, rising well above the cab, with a small checkered flag plane near the top.

I'll skip the tailgate stripe decals and fender guards for now, keeping things simple. I'm adding gold bolt accents on the rims and headlight trim, and considering a steel belly skid plate positioned to clear the driveshaft, checking the frame rail gap against the body clearance to make sure nothing collides.

Now I'm placing body mount boxes at the frame corners to bridge that gap, then extending the rails front and rear for a bumper overhang, and laying out the axle tubes with planetary hub detailing near the rim.

Checking for collisions, I'm nudging the shock mounts inward off the axle centerline so they clear the tire's inner face, then sizing the portal housing boxes to sit snugly against the narrowed axle tube width.

Adjusting shock position to x=1.09 with spring radius 0.085, which keeps it just touching the body at 1.0 without clipping. Now placing the top mount bracket where the shock attaches to the body side.

Adding the lower mounting rod, then laying out the four-link suspension bars with lower and upper links connecting axle to rails, plus a panhard/steering rod, and starting the axle diff housing.

Skipping the hood, I'm working out chrome exhaust pipes running along the sides, sweeping from near the hood down past the body, checking they don't collide with the tires at that x-position.

I realize the side pipes actually do collide with the shock bracket near the spring top, so I'll drop them and rely on rear exhaust stacks instead. I'm also skipping mud flaps and winch hooks, but adding small yellow fog lights on the front bumper face and a red tow hook box positioned near the bumper edges.

Deciding to skip the bull bar and push bar sweep for the front, and skip sidewall lettering too, though I'll keep a yellow accent ring on the tire sidewall. For pixel consistency I'm standardizing the texel size across tire and body decals, then setting up wheel center coordinates with a sign function for outward direction.

Writing tire paint function...

Within that closure, I'm computing radial distance and angle from the cell's position relative to the wheel center to distinguish cap cells from tread cells based on the normal's x-component, then building a gold gradient ramp for the hub cap when close to the center.

Working through more ring zones...

For shoulder lugs I'm shading darker or lighter based on position, then adding mud effects near the bottom of the tire using noise and random speckling with a brown dirt color. For the tread pattern, I'm setting the chevron lug color against a darker base, layering in mud speckles weighted by vertical position, and computing the chevron phase using angle plus horizontal offset to get the correct diagonal slope across the tread width.

Now I'm working out the boundary between sidewall and rim: the tire cylinder has one radius/width and the rim cylinder another, with the rim mostly hidden inside the tire but protruding slightly on each side. Since the rim's surface normals fall in a smaller radius range, I'm adding a check early in the color logic so any point with small radius and within the axial band gets painted as steel rim rather than tread.

Now I'm sketching out the actual part-creation calls, using cylinder geometries with paint functions and position/rotation parameters, sharing paint objects like BODY and CAB across tileBox parts, and importing the Cell type from the pixel kit module.

I'm defining a color palette for the truck's blue body and flame decal (yellow, orange, red), plus a triangle-wave helper function, then writing a bodyFn that computes mud staining based on vertical position using noise.

Now I'm adding the mud splatter probability logic for the lower body panel, then layering on a dark rocker trim strip below it, and finally sketching a racing stripe on the roof based on horizontal distance from center.

Now I'm working out flame decal placement on the side panels using a triangular wave pattern across the lower slab height to create yellow-orange-red flame gradients.

For the darkest outline value I'll shade it near a deep red-black. Otherwise I'm blending blue tones based on surface normal with added noise texture and dithered color picking, then starting to define the cab function that checks which side a cell is on to determine glass placement.

Still writing glass conditions... defining windshield, side window, and rear window regions by height and position bounds, falling back to the body shading function when a cell isn't glass, and leaving the roof area to the existing stripe logic in bodyFn.

Now I'm placing the taillights and rear license plate on the bumper and slab rear faces, positioning the plate above the bumper at the correct depth, then checking how the lower slab's top surface relates to the bed floor for the tailgate area.

I'm skipping finer details like fuel caps, cab ladders, wheel arches, and brake discs since they're minor and the body already clears the tyres fine. For the headlights, I'm layering a dark steel rim box slightly in front of the face plane at the front z-position, and considering whether to add amber marker lights along the cab roof's front edge as a light bar.

Thinking about parts count, I'm aiming for roughly 120 pieces, with richer details like merged shock coil rings (8 shocks × 9 rings, merged per shock to save geometry), rivet rows along bed walls and bumpers, hood pins, and door handles—while skipping seats, steering rack, and brake calipers to keep things efficient.

Now I'm double-checking that all tires sit at or near ground level with no clipping, and setting the height progression for the roof, light bar, exhaust stacks, and antenna tip up to the flag. I'm also working out the rod function signature for building tube-shaped parts like shocks and antennas, considering whether to use a hexagonal cross-section for a pixel-art look with flat end caps.

Building spring coils and shock absorber tubes...

Still assembling geometry...

I'm now mirroring parts across both sides using sign loops, then building the frame rails and cross members with dark steel coloring, plus axle and diff cover colors in contrasting grey tones.

Building box helper function...

Generating more pixel textures...

Positioning the light bar panels and mounting feet on the roof, then adding fog lights on the front bumper and a row of chrome rivets along the bumper's top edge, plus bed items like nitro bottles.

I'm adding dark rim caps along the bed rail tops, then working out exhaust stack placement, adjusting the rear hoop position to z -1.0 and stacks to z -0.72 so they clear the cab rear wall without overlapping, and adding heat-shield bands around the stacks.

Now I'm defining the hoop's corner points and chrome rod radius, plus diagonal braces running backward to mounts near the cab rear, figuring out how the hoop and stacks interplay given their offset z-depths.

I realize the stacks at x 0.8 collide with the hoop brace near the cab, so I'm shifting the stacks inward to x ±0.5 to avoid the overlap while keeping their tilt. I'm also positioning the antenna as a thin rod mounted at the tailgate corner, running up from the bed wall with a small ball tip.

Now I'm placing a flag on the antenna rod, sized and centered to hang correctly, then adding skull decals on both bed walls at a matched position and size. I'm also considering adding a pinstripe and door-seam lines along the lower cab body for extra detail, since the flame graphics only cover the lower section.

I'm restricting the seam line to the cab region only, checking that it stays within the valid y-range and x-facing normal, then confirming the bed floor tile pattern is set with the diamond texture at the right scale. Still deciding on wheel mud flaps and hub details.

Now I'm setting up the module structure: adding metadata (name, description, style, commit), defining the default export build function that creates the object via createBuilder and returns the root group, and pulling in necessary imports like noise, paint types, catmull-rom path helper, and geometry merging utilities. I'm confirming the noise function signature takes a position vector, size, and seed, then starting a helper function for generating tire bolt rings.

Writing bolt geometry code...

Now I'm planning the bed wall rivets along the top rim and the tailgate box placement, then composing the final mesh with all these detail parts merged together.
